claim: In Shaker K+ channels, the S4-S5 linker couples the voltage sensor (VSD) and pore domain (PD).
source: In Shaker K+ channels, the S4-S5 linker couples the voltage sensor (VSD) and pore domain (PD).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the abstract and is supported by citations in the introduction.

claim: In L361R:W434F channels, W434F affects the L361R VSD seen as a shallower charge-voltage (Q-V) curve that crosses the conductance-voltage (G-V) curve.
source: In L361R:W434F, W434F affects the L361R VSD seen as a shallower charge-voltage (Q-V) curve that crosses the conductance-voltage (G-V) curve.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B and described in the results section.

claim: In L366H:W434F channels, L366H relieves the W434F effect converting a non-conductive channel into a conductive one.
source: In L366H:W434F, L366H relieves the W434F effect converting a non-conductive channel in a conductive one.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3 and described in the results section.

claim: A chain of residues connects the VSD (S4) to the selectivity filter (SF) in the PD of an adjacent subunit as the molecular basis for voltage sensor selectivity filter gate (VS-SF) coupling.
source: We report a chain of residues connecting the VSD (S4) to the selectivity filter (SF) in the PD of an adjacent subunit as the molecular basis for voltage sensor selectivity filter gate (VS-SF) coupling.
evidence: This is the main finding of the study, supported by multiple experimental data and structural models shown in Figures 1-6.

claim: Single alanine substitutions at L409A, S411A, S412A, or F433A are sufficient to disrupt the VS-SF coupling in L361R:W434F mutant channels.
source: Single alanine substitutions in this region (L409A, S411A, S412A, or F433A) are enough to disrupt the VS-SF coupling, shown by the absence of Q-V and G-V crossing in L361R:W434F mutant
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C-F and Table 1.

claim: Single alanine substitutions at L409A, S411A, or S412A eliminate ionic conduction in L366H:W434F mutant channels.
source: Single alanine substitutions in this region (L409A, S411A, S412A, or F433A) are enough to disrupt the VS-SF coupling, shown by the absence of Q-V and G-V crossing in L361R:W434F mutant and by the lack of ionic conduction in the L366H:W434F mutant.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4 and described in the results section.

claim: Voltage-gated potassium channels (KV) are responsible for the repolarization phase of the action potential.
source: Voltage-gated potassium channels (KV) are members of the voltage-gated ion channels superfamily, responsible for the repolarization phase of the action potential, for maximal action potential firing frequency and for simply keeping the membrane potential negative in non-excitable cells.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about the physiological role of KV channels.

claim: KV channels are assembled as homotetramers.
source: In general, KV channels are assembled as homotetramers.
evidence: This is established structural knowledge about KV channels.

claim: Each KV channel subunit monomer contains a voltage sensor domain (VSD) formed by transmembrane segments S1-S4.
source: Each subunit monomer contains two functional domains: the voltage sensor domain (VSD), formed by transmembrane segments S1-S4
evidence: This is established structural knowledge about KV channels.

claim: Each KV channel subunit monomer contains a pore domain (PD) composed by transmembrane segments S5, P-loop, and S6.
source: the pore domain (PD), composed by transmembrane segments S5, P-loop (a reentrant region in the protein), and S6.
evidence: This is established structural knowledge about KV channels.

claim: There are two tetramerized architectures identified among KV channels: domain-swapped channels and non-domain-swapped channels.
source: Presently, there are two tetramerized architectures identified among KV channels: domain-swapped channels (KV1.2 [Long et al., 2005a] and KV7.1 [Sun and MacKinnon, 2017]) and non-domain-swapped channels (EAG1 [Whicher and MacKinnon, 2016], HERG [Wang and MacKinnon, 2017], HCN [Lee and MacKinnon, 2017], BK [Tao et al., 2017], KVAP [Tao and MacKinnon, 2019], and KAT1 [Clark et al., 2020]).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to structural studies of different KV channels.

claim: In domain-swapped channels, the VSD from one subunit is in close contact with the PD from a neighboring subunit.
source: In domain-swapped channels, the VSD from one subunit is in close contact with the PD from a neighboring subunit, forming an extensive inter-subunit non-covalent interface.
evidence: This is established structural knowledge about domain-swapped KV channels, supported by citations.

claim: In non-domain-swapped channels, the VSD and the PD from the same subunit form a non-covalent interface and are connected by a shorter version of the S4-S5 linker.
source: In non-domain-swapped channels, the VSD and the PD from the same subunit forms a similar non-covalent interface and the domains are connected by a shorter version of the S4-S5 linker.
evidence: This is established structural knowledge about non-domain-swapped KV channels, supported by citations.

claim: S4 movements driven by changes in membrane potential lead to changes in S4-S5 linker position, which results in the opening or closing of the channel inner gate.
source: According to a well-studied electromechanical coupling mechanism, henceforth canonical coupling for simplicity, S4 movements driven by changes in the membrane potential lead to changes in S4-S5 linker position, which results in the opening or closing of channel inner gate (bundle crossing), at the intracellular end of the permeation pathway (Kalstrup and Blunck, 2018; Long et al., 2005a; Long et al., 2005b; Lu et al., 2002).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the canonical coupling mechanism, supported by multiple citations.

claim: For a channel that opens as the voltage is made more positive, Q-V curves typically appear to the left of the G-V curves in the voltage axis.
source: Therefore, for a channel that opens as the voltage is made more positive, Q-V curves typically appear to the left of the G-V curves in the voltage axis.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the relationship between gating currents and ionic currents in voltage-gated channels.

claim: W434F is a mutation known to abrogate ionic K+ currents by increasing the speed of C-type inactivation.
source: W434F is a well-studied mutation, known to abrogate ionic K+ currents by increasing the speed of C-type inactivation (Perozo et al., 1993; Yang et al., 1997)
evidence: This is established knowledge about the W434F mutation, supported by citations.

claim: W434F mutation is widely used to record gating currents in Shaker channels.
source: it is also widely used to record gating currents in Shaker channels (Bezanilla, 2018).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the experimental use of W434F mutation, supported by citation.

claim: The L361R-W434F interaction was revealed by an unusual crossing between the Q-V curve from L361R:W434F channels and the G-V curve from L361R channels.
source: The L361R-W434F interaction was revealed by an unusual crossing between the Q-V curve (from L361R:W434F channels) and the G-V curve (from L361R channels) (Carvalho-de-Souza and Bezanilla, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study and by data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The Q-V and G-V crossing does not occur when the Q-V curve is estimated from L361R channels in the absence of W434F and after depleting K+ ions.
source: However, this did not occur when the Q-V curve was estimated from L361R channels, in the absence of W434F and after depleting K+ ions.
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study and by data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The VSD and the PD are likely communicating by an alternative pathway, other than through the S4-S5 linker.
source: This suggests that the VSD and the PD are likely communicating by an alternative pathway, other than through the S4-S5 linker.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental observations of L361R:W434F channels and supported by citations to related studies.

claim: An alternative coupling pathway between VSD and PD has been observed in Shaker channels.
source: Such an alternative pathway has been observed in Shaker (Carvalho-de-Souza and Bezanilla, 2019; Conti et al., 2016; Fernández-Mariño et al., 2018) and in KV7.1 (Hou et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: An alternative coupling pathway between VSD and PD has been observed in KV7.1 channels.
source: Such an alternative pathway has been observed in Shaker (Carvalho-de-Souza and Bezanilla, 2019; Conti et al., 2016; Fernández-Mariño et al., 2018) and in KV7.1 (Hou et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: The alternative coupling pathway in Shaker operates independent of the canonical coupling.
source: In Shaker, a domain-swapped channel (Carvalho-de-Souza and Bezanilla, 2019) showed that this alternative pathway operates independent of the canonical coupling.
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: The alternative coupling mechanism is mediated by the interface of contact between the VSD and the PD from different subunits.
source: In fact, it was found to be mediated by the interface of contact between the VSD and the PD from different subunits.
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: The noncanonical coupling mechanism endows voltage dependence to the SF gate.
source: They classified this mechanism as noncanonical and demonstrated that it endows voltage dependence to the SF gate.
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: The proposed chain of residues for VS-SF coupling includes V363, L366, or V369 at the VSD end, depending on the relative position of S4.
source: At the VSD end, depending on the relative position of the S4, the series of residues starts with V363, L366, or V369.
evidence: This is based on structural models and previous hypotheses, as indicated by the citation.

claim: The proposed chain of residues for VS-SF coupling includes L409, S411, and S412 in S5.
source: Next, comes L409, S411, and S412 in S5
evidence: This is based on structural models and previous hypotheses, as indicated by the citation.

claim: The proposed chain of residues for VS-SF coupling includes F433 and W434 in the P-loop.
source: F433, and W434 in the P-loop
evidence: This is based on structural models and previous hypotheses, as indicated by the citation.

claim: The proposed chain of residues for VS-SF coupling includes Y445 in the SF.
source: at last, Y445 in the SF.
evidence: This is based on structural models and previous hypotheses, as indicated by the citation.

claim: From the KV1.2 structure, it is possible to appreciate the close contact between the proposed chain of residues.
source: From the KV1.2 structure (Chen et al., 2010; Long et al., 2005a), it is possible to appreciate the close contact between these residues.
evidence: This is supported by citations to structural studies and by Figure 1.

claim: All alanine substitutions on L361R:W434F channels restored the normal position of the Q-V curve with respect to the G-V curve.
source: All alanine substitutions restored the normal position of the Q-V curve with respect to the G-V curve.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C-F and Table 1.

claim: All alanine substitutions on L366H:W434F channels were sufficient to decrease the K+ conduction to levels comparable to the W434F phenotype.
source: Interestingly, all alanine substitutions on L366H:W434F channels were sufficient to decrease the K+ conduction to levels comparable to the W434F phenotype.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4.

claim: The VS-SF coupling comprises the proposed chain of residues in domain-swapped channels.
source: Together, these results demonstrate that the VS-SF coupling (1) comprises the proposed chain of residues, in domain-swapped channels
evidence: This is the conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in the study.

claim: The VS-SF coupling is dependent on the volume of the chain residues.
source: (2) is dependent on the volume of these residues
evidence: This is the conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing that alanine substitutions (which reduce side chain volume) disrupt the coupling.

claim: The VSD affects the dynamics of the SF gate.
source: (3) reveals that the VSD affects the dynamics of the SF gate
evidence: This is the conclusion drawn from the experimental data, particularly from the L361R:W434F results.

claim: The SF gate affects the movement of the VSD.
source: and that the SF gate affects the movement of the VSD.
evidence: This is the conclusion drawn from the experimental data, particularly from the L361R:W434F results showing Q-V curve shifts.

claim: Q-V and G-V curves do not cross each other when any of the alanine substitutions (L409A, S411A, S412A, F433A) are performed in the presence of the W434F mutation in L361R:W434F background.
source: We found that Q-V and G-V curves do not cross each other when any of the alanine substitutions are performed in the presence of the W434F mutation (Figure 2A-F, Table 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2 and Table 1.

claim: The side chain volume in residues L409, S411, S412, and F433 is the base for the communication between the SF and the VSD.
source: This indicates that the side chain volume in residues L409, S411, S412, and F433 is the base for the communication between the SF and the VSD.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental observation that alanine substitutions (which reduce side chain volume) disrupt the coupling.

claim: Q-V curves from all mutants containing L361R were satisfactorily fitted with a two-state model equation.
source: The Q-V curves from all mutants containing L361R were satisfactorily fitted with a two-state model equation and the best-fitted values for all curves used in this study are summarized in Table 1.
evidence: This is a description of the data analysis method used, with results shown in Table 1.

claim: A two-state model equation can satisfactorily fit Q-V curves from sensors that appear to populate three or more conformational states during activation, but it does so by underestimating the total gating charges per sensor.
source: A two-state model equation can satisfactory fit Q-V curves from sensors that appear to populate three or more conformational states during activation, but it does so by underestimating the total gating charges per sensor (Bezanilla and Villalba-Galea, 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the limitations of two-state model fitting, supported by citation.

claim: W434F may stabilize the resting state of L361R VSD channel, affecting the VSD activation and/or deactivation, seen as a right shift in the Q-V curve.
source: Another possibility is that the W434F stabilizes the resting state of L361R VSD channel, affecting the VSD activation and/or deactivation, seen as a right shift in the Q-V curve.
evidence: This is speculation about the mechanism underlying the observed Q-V curve shift.

claim: Channels bearing L361R mutations may have more closed states than WT channels.
source: Altogether, it may be possible that channels bearing L361R mutations have more closed states than WT channels (an issue we did not pursue further in the present study).
evidence: This is speculation based on the fitting results, but not pursued experimentally.

claim: L366H:W434F channels show gating currents followed by a slower rising current consistent with a K+ conductance.
source: Currents recorded from L366H:W434F channels appear to be highly expressed, as they clearly show gating currents followed by a slower rising current consistent with a K+ conductance 1–2 times larger (Figure 3a–c).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3a-c.

claim: L366H:W434F channels have a much smaller macroscopic conductance to gating currents ratio than wild-type channels.
source: This is, however, a much smaller macroscopic conductance to gating currents ratio than in wild-type channels (typically two orders of magnitude or more).
evidence: This is inferred from comparison of the experimental data with known properties of wild-type channels.

claim: L366H:W434F channels have dramatically decreased unitary conductance and/or open probability.
source: These data indicate that, although L366H:W434F channels are conductive, their unitary conductance and/or open probability are dramatically decreased.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation of small ionic currents relative to gating currents.

claim: The currents through L366H:W434F channels represent K+ moving through the permeation pathway of the PD and not through an omega pore.
source: Several features of the ionic currents carried by the L366H:W434F channels indicate that they represent K+ moving through the permeation pathway of the PD and not through an eventual omega pore as in some Shaker mutants (Tombola et al., 2005)
evidence: This is inferred from multiple experimental observations described in the text and supported by citation.

claim: The currents through L366H:W434F channels are not carried by protons.
source: or being carried by protons as it happens with some other His mutations in the VSD (Starace and Bezanilla, 2004).
evidence: This is inferred from multiple experimental observations described in the text and supported by citation.

claim: L366H:W434F channels show a decay under sustained voltage-clamp depolarization reminiscent of C-type inactivation.
source: First, the currents in the L366H:W434F mutant show a decay under sustained voltage-clamp depolarization reminiscent of C-type inactivation, suggesting this process has not been eliminated but rather mitigated (Figure 3a,b).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3a,b.

claim: The currents through L366H:W434F channels were blocked by 1 mM of 4-aminopyridine (4-AP).
source: Second, the currents were blocked by 1 mM of 4-aminopyridine (4-AP) (Figure 3c,d), a broad-spectrum K+ channel pore blocker (Kirsch et al., 1993).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3c,d and by citation.

claim: 4-aminopyridine (4-AP) is a broad-spectrum K+ channel pore blocker.
source: a broad-spectrum K+ channel pore blocker (Kirsch et al., 1993).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: The currents through L366H:W434F channels are K+-selective as revealed by their reversal potential in different K+ gradients.
source: Third, the currents through L366H:W434F channels are K+-selective as revealed by their reversal potential in different K+ gradients (Figure 3a,b,d).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3a,b,d.

claim: The maximal conductance of L366H:W434F channels in symmetrical K+ solutions was approximately threefold larger than the conductance in asymmetrical K+ solutions.
source: Moreover, the maximal conductance in symmetrical K+ solutions was approximately threefold larger than the conductance in asymmetrical K+ solutions (Figure 3e).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3e.

claim: Under symmetrical K+ concentrations (140 mM), the open probability (Po) of Shaker-IR-W434F is 100-fold higher compared to the absence of external K+.
source: It has been reported that under symmetrical K+ concentrations (140 mM), the open probability (Po) of Shaker-IR-W434F is a 100-fold higher as compared to the absence of external K+ (10−7 vs. 10−5) with no expected changes in the single channel conductance (Yang et al., 1997).
evidence: This is established knowledge from a previous study, supported by citation.

claim: An increase in the number of channels available to open was observed in C-type inactivation enhanced mutants of Shaker (e.g. T449A, T449E, T449K).
source: In a different study, an increase in the number of channels available to open was observed in C-type inactivation enhanced mutants of Shaker (e.g. T449A, T449E, T449K) (López-Barneo et al., 1993).
evidence: This is established knowledge from a previous study, supported by citation.

claim: The increased conductance in higher external K+ in L366H:W434F channels is interpreted as a combination of the increase in the open probability and the increase of the number of channels that open under depolarization.
source: Therefore, we interpret the increased conductance in higher external K+ in L366H:W434F channels as a combination of the increase in the open probability and the increase of the number of channels that open under depolarization, which appears to be a common feature in C-type inactivation enhanced mutants of Shaker.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the experimental data and previous knowledge from cited studies.

claim: G-V curves from L366H mutants in the absence and in the presence of W434F mutation have very similar voltage dependency and voltage sensitivity.
source: Moreover, G-V curves from L366H mutants in the absence and in the presence of W434F mutation have very similar voltage dependency and voltage sensitivity (Figure 3f, Table 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3f and Table 1.

claim: The canonical coupling underlying channel gating seems to be unaltered in L366H:W434F double mutant.
source: This observation further reinforces the notion that the PD of L366H:W434F channels is conductive and suggests that the canonical coupling underlying channel gating seems to be unaltered in this double mutant.
evidence: This is inferred from the similarity of G-V curves with and without W434F in L366H background.

claim: Q-V curves measured in L366H channels with V478W mutation or W434F (after conductance blockade by 4-AP) are practically identical.
source: Q-V curves measured in L366H channels with V478W mutation, that prevents inner gate (bundle crossing) opening (Kitaguchi et al., 2004) or W434F (after conductance blockade by 4-AP), are also practically identical (Figure 3g – Table 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3g and Table 1, and by citation.

claim: V478W mutation prevents inner gate (bundle crossing) opening.
source: V478W mutation, that prevents inner gate (bundle crossing) opening (Kitaguchi et al., 2004)
evidence: This is established knowledge from a previous study, supported by citation.

claim: The W434F mutation does not affect VSD movements in the particular case of L366H-mutant VSD.
source: This implies that the W434F mutation does not affect VSD movements in the particular case of L366H-mutant VSD.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Q-V curves are identical with V478W or W434F in L366H background.

claim: Mutating L409, S411, or S412 to alanine in L366H:W434F channels greatly depressed the K+ currents leaving only gating currents to be observed.
source: Consistently, mutating L409, S411, or S412 to alanine in L366H:W434F channels, the K+ currents were greatly depressed leaving only gating currents to be observed (Figure 4).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Peak of ionic currents from all triple mutants (L366H with L409A, S411A, or S412A and W434F) were remarkably small (to ~0.3 µA at 60 mV).
source: Peak of ionic currents from all triple mutants were remarkably small (to ~0.3 µA at 60 mV), indicating L409, S411, and S412 are also involved in the VS-SF coupling in L366H:W434F channels.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4.

claim: L409, S411, and S412 are involved in the VS-SF coupling in L366H:W434F channels.
source: indicating L409, S411, and S412 are also involved in the VS-SF coupling in L366H:W434F channels.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that alanine substitutions at these positions eliminate K+ currents in L366H:W434F channels.

claim: The weighted inactivation time constant (τInac) for F433A was essentially identical to WT.
source: While the τInac was essentially identical for F433A and WT, it was considerably slower for L409A, S411A, and S412A (Figure 5f).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5f.

claim: The weighted inactivation time constant (τInac) was considerably slower for L409A, S411A, and S412A compared to WT.
source: While the τInac was essentially identical for F433A and WT, it was considerably slower for L409A, S411A, and S412A (Figure 5f).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5f.

claim: The fraction of the fast component of the inactivation for L409A and S411A was smaller when compared to WT.
source: The fraction of the fast component of the inactivation for L409A and S411A was smaller when compared to WT, but similar for S412A and F433A (Figure 5g).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5g.

claim: The fraction of the fast component of the inactivation for S412A and F433A was similar to WT.
source: The fraction of the fast component of the inactivation for L409A and S411A was smaller when compared to WT, but similar for S412A and F433A (Figure 5g).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5g.

claim: Some of the alanine substitutions (L409A, S411A, and F433A) led to significant right shifts both in the G-V curve and in the Inac-V curve.
source: Some of the alanine substitutions (L409A, S411A, and F433A) led to significant right shifts both in the G-V curve and in the available current after several different inactivating voltages pulses (Inac-V curve) (see Figure 5h–l and Table 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5h-l and Table 1.

claim: The Q-V curves from L409A, S411A, and F433A mutants were not right-shifted.
source: The corresponding Q-V curves from those mutants, on the other hand, were not right-shifted, suggesting that those replaced residues exert a significant role in the VSD to pore conduction coupling in regular channels.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5h-l and Table 1.

claim: Residues L409, S411, and F433 exert a significant role in the VSD to pore conduction coupling in regular channels.
source: suggesting that those replaced residues exert a significant role in the VSD to pore conduction coupling in regular channels.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that alanine substitutions at these positions shift G-V and Inac-V curves but not Q-V curves.

claim: Only F433A led to a significant change in the energy of the second transition of the Q-V curve (~1.7 kcal/mol).
source: Among all alanine substitutions, only F433A led to a significant change in the energy of the second transition of the Q-V curve (~1.7 kcal/mol – Figure 5m).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data and analysis shown in Figure 5m.

claim: For the energy associated to the conductance process, only mutation S412A did not lead to a significant change.
source: For the energy associated to the conductance process, only mutation S412A did not lead to a significant change (Figure 5n).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data and analysis shown in Figure 5n.

claim: Only mutation S411A did not lead to a significant change in the energy related to the inactivation process.
source: Whereas only mutation S411A did not lead to a significant change in the energy related to the inactivation process (Figure 5o).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data and analysis shown in Figure 5o.

claim: Apart from F433A, alanine substitutions in the VS-SF coupling have little or no effect in the dynamics of WT VSD.
source: Altogether, from these results we learned that, apart from F433A, alanine substitutions in the VS-SF coupling have little or no effect in the dynamics of WT VSD.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Residues L409, S411, S412, and F433 are crucially important for the channel VSD to pore conduction coupling.
source: Nevertheless, those same residues are crucially important for the channel VSD to pore conduction coupling.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing effects on G-V and Inac-V curves.

claim: The VSD to pore conduction coupling involves both activation and inactivation processes.
source: It involves both activation and inactivation processes even though the overall effects were small.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing effects on both G-V and Inac-V curves.

claim: The available current at very positive voltages was considerably increased when mutations S412A and F433A are present in the channels.
source: Notably, the available current at very positive voltages was considerably increased when mutations S412A and F433A are present in the channels (Figure 5h,k and l), showing the importance of the residues to stabilize the inactivation conformation at the SF.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5h,k,l.

claim: Residues S412 and F433 are important to stabilize the inactivation conformation at the SF.
source: showing the importance of the residues to stabilize the inactivation conformation at the SF.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that mutations at these positions increase available current at positive voltages.

claim: The V478W mutation prevents ionic conduction.
source: To record gating currents by a mechanism that does not involve the SF and W434F, we used the V478W mutation at the bundle crossing region. This mutation prevents ionic conduction (Kitaguchi et al., 2004; Pau et al., 2017)
evidence: This is established knowledge from previous studies, supported by citations.

claim: The V478W mutation does not affect the movement of the VSD.
source: and does not affect the movement of the VSD (Kitaguchi et al., 2004).
evidence: This is established knowledge from a previous study, supported by citation.

claim: The interaction between S411 and F433 is +2.00 ± 0.76 kcal/mol.
source: The interaction between S411 and F433 is +2.00 ± 0.76 kcal/mol and is above the cutoff value of 1.8 kcal/mol, as previously established for this kind of analysis (Chowdhury et al., 2014; Fernández-Mariño et al., 2018).
evidence: This is calculated from experimental data using the thermodynamic mutant cycle analysis shown in Figure 6 and Table 2.

claim: The interaction energy between S411 and F433 is above the cutoff value of 1.8 kcal/mol for significant interaction.
source: The interaction between S411 and F433 is +2.00 ± 0.76 kcal/mol and is above the cutoff value of 1.8 kcal/mol, as previously established for this kind of analysis (Chowdhury et al., 2014; Fernández-Mariño et al., 2018).
evidence: This is based on established criteria from previous studies, supported by citations.

claim: The connecting chain operates in the WT channels, independent of the presence of W434F mutation.
source: Therefore, this data supports that the connecting chain operates in the WT channels, independent of the presence of W434F mutation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the thermodynamic mutant cycle analysis showing interaction between S411 and F433 in the absence of W434F.

claim: Several lines of evidence have pointed to the existence of different coupling mechanisms between the VSD and the PD in Shaker channels.
source: Recently, several lines of evidence have pointed to the existence of different coupling mechanisms between the VSD and the PD in Shaker channels (Fernández-Mariño et al., 2018; Conti et al., 2016; Carvalho-de-Souza and Bezanilla, 2019; Petitjean et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: These coupling mechanisms extend beyond the canonical electromechanical S4-S5 linker-based coupling.
source: These mechanisms extend beyond the canonical electromechanical S4-S5 linker-based coupling.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: A chain of amino acid residues is determinant for an alternative coupling in Shaker.
source: In this study, we demonstrate that a chain of amino acid residues is determinant for an alternative coupling in Shaker.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study, supported by the experimental data presented.

claim: Three residues in the S5 segment (L409, S411, S412) and two in the P-loop (F433, W434) are key for the VS-SF coupling.
source: Three residues in the S5 segment (L409, S411, S412) and two in the P-loop (F433, W434) are key for this functional VS-SF coupling.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study, supported by the experimental data presented.

claim: The VSD and the PD involved in the VS-SF coupling chain are conformationally coupled through adjacent subunits.
source: Crucially, the VSD and the PD involved in this chain are conformationally coupled through adjacent subunits.
evidence: This is based on the structural models shown in Figure 1 and the experimental data.

claim: Other paths for VSD-PD coupling may also exist beyond the identified chain.
source: Yet, we must consider the fact that these aforementioned residues may not be the only ones involved in these processes, as it is possible that other paths may also exist (Conti et al., 2016; Lee et al., 2009).
evidence: This is speculation based on citations to previous studies.

claim: The observation of L361R:W434F and L366H:W434F cases shows the bidirectionality of the putative VS-SF coupling between the VSD and the PD.
source: The observation of these cases is quite remarkable because it shows the bidirectionality of the putative VS-SF coupling between the VSD and the PD.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental observations that VSD mutations affect SF properties and SF mutations affect VSD properties.

claim: All observations showing an exacerbated VS-SF coupling were done in the presence of the W434F mutation.
source: It is important to notice that all our observations showing an exacerbated VS-SF coupling were done in the presence of the W434F mutation.
evidence: This is a statement about the experimental design and conditions.

claim: The VS-SF coupling mechanism is always present and independent of the presence of W434F mutation.
source: Our data suggest that the mechanism is in fact always present (Figures 5 and 6) and it is independent of the presence of W434F mutation
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data shown in Figures 5 and 6.

claim: The W434F mutation makes the VS-SF coupling more conspicuous because this mutation significantly enhances C-type inactivation.
source: however, the W434F mutation makes it more conspicuous because this mutation significantly enhances C-type inactivation (Yang et al., 1997).
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the experimental data and previous knowledge from cited study.

claim: There is a detectable coupling path between the VSD and the PD, as outlined in Figure 1.
source: Therefore, the roles of these chained residues on the overall VSD to pore opening coupling mechanism in regular Shaker channels are validated. Indeed, these results when combined demonstrate that there is a detectable coupling path between the VSD and the PD, as outlined in Figure 1.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study, supported by all the experimental data and Figure 1.

claim: F244C mutation in S1 segment of Shaker channels produces a similar relief in the W434F-induced inactivation.
source: Recently, a different study has shown that F244C, a mutation in S1 segment of Shaker channels, also produces a similar relief in the W434F-induced inactivation: the double mutant F244C:W434F also conducts K+ and the current is blocked by 4-AP (Petitjean et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge from a previous study, supported by citation.

claim: F244 is one of the residues forming the hydrophobic plug in Shaker channels.
source: F244, one of the residues forming the hydrophobic plug in Shaker channels (Lacroix et al., 2014), is in close proximity to residue S412 (Chen et al., 2010) from a PD of a neighboring subunit.
evidence: This is established knowledge from previous studies, supported by citations.

claim: F244 is in close proximity to residue S412 from a PD of a neighboring subunit.
source: F244, one of the residues forming the hydrophobic plug in Shaker channels (Lacroix et al., 2014), is in close proximity to residue S412 (Chen et al., 2010) from a PD of a neighboring subunit.
evidence: This is based on structural information from a previous study, supported by citation.

claim: The interaction between F244C and W434F would take place via the VS-SF coupling.
source: Thus, under our proposal, the interaction between F244C and W434F would take place via the VS-SF coupling as well.
evidence: This is inferred from the proximity of F244 to S412 and the experimental observations.

claim: The F244C homolog in KV1.1, F184C, causes episodic ataxia in human patients.
source: Consistently, the F244C homolog in KV1.1, F184C, causes episodic ataxia in human patients (Browne et al., 1995).
evidence: This is established clinical knowledge from a previous study, supported by citation.

claim: Mutations in human KV channels at the S412 equivalent have neurological consequences in KV1.1 and KV7.2.
source: Mutations in human KV channels at the S412 equivalent have neurological (in KV1.1 [Lee et al., 2004] and KV7.2 [Dedek et al., 2003])
evidence: This is established clinical knowledge from previous studies, supported by citations.

claim: Mutations in human KV channels at the S412 equivalent have cardiac consequences in KV7.1.
source: and cardiac (in KV7.1 [Liu et al., 2002]) consequences in humans.
evidence: This is established clinical knowledge from a previous study, supported by citation.

claim: In Shaker channel, the residue I470 is a key participant in the coupling between the activation gate and C-type inactivation.
source: In Shaker channel, the residue I470 is a key participant in the coupling between the activation gate, at the bundle crossing region, and C-type inactivation (Peters et al., 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge from a previous study, supported by citation.

claim: I470 interacts with T442 in the signature sequence of K+-selective channels at the SF.
source: It has been proposed that I470 interacts with T442, in the signature sequence of K+-selective channels, TVGYG, at the SF (Labro et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism from a previous study, supported by citation.

claim: The I470-T442 interaction constitutes an indirect pathway that couples the voltage sensor with the inner gate and the SF.
source: This mechanism constitutes an indirect pathway that couples the voltage sensor with the inner gate and the SF.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the cited study.

claim: Several studies have shown that mutations in the outer mouth of the pore, S5 segment and P-loop, affect C-type inactivation.
source: Several studies have shown that mutations in the outer mouth of the pore, S5 segment and P-loop, affect C-type inactivation, highlighting the importance of these motifs for the inactivation process (De Biasi et al., 1993; Larsson and Elinder, 2000; Molina et al., 1997; Ortega-Sáenz et al., 2000; Perozo et al., 1993; Yang et al., 1997).
evidence: This is established knowledge from multiple previous studies, supported by citations.

claim: There is a direct interaction between the voltage sensor and the SF mediated by the VS-SF coupling mechanism.
source: These studies and our data demonstrate the existence of a direct interaction between the voltage sensor and the SF mediated by the mechanism proposed here.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data and previous studies.

claim: The canonical coupling mechanism is the main mechanism whereby the channels' pore is gated by the VSD.
source: Presently, we do not have data to support a definite answer for these questions, but it seems that the canonical coupling mechanism is the main mechanism whereby the channels' pore is gated by the VSD.
evidence: This is speculation based on the experimental observations and general knowledge.

claim: Inter-subunit metal bridges between residues V476C and H486 tend to stabilize the channels in the open conformation.
source: Inter-subunit metal bridges between residues V476C and H486 tend to stabilize the channels in the open conformation, displaying K+ currents without apparent activation kinetics, as expected in the absence of a voltage-dependent gating process (Holmgren et al., 1998).
evidence: This is established knowledge from a previous study, supported by citation.

claim: The closure of the activation gate is essential for the recovery from C-type inactivation.
source: A recent study, using T449A:V476C Shaker background and metal bridges, has concluded that the closure of the activation gate (where the canonical coupling mechanism operates) is essential for the recovery from C-type inactivation (Szanto et al., 2020).
evidence: This is established knowledge from a recent study, supported by citation.

claim: The VS-SF coupling, by itself, is not sufficient to gate the channel's inner gate.
source: This suggests that the VS-SF coupling, by itself, is not sufficient to gate the channel's inner gate and, consequently, the channel.
evidence: This is inferred from the cited study showing that activation gate closure is essential for recovery from inactivation.

claim: Mutations in the bundle crossing region have shown that the pore stays open and does not close even when very negative potentials are applied.
source: Furthermore, mutations in the bundle crossing region have shown that the pore stays open and does not close even when very negative potentials are applied (Kitaguchi et al., 2004).
evidence: This is established knowledge from a previous study, supported by citation.

claim: The VS-SF coupling cannot, by itself, transfer enough energy to the PD in order to gate the channel.
source: It is reasonable to believe that the VS-SF coupling cannot, by itself, transfer enough energy to the PD in order to gate the channel, pointing to the notion that it is an accessory or modulatory gating mechanism.
evidence: This is speculation based on the experimental observations and cited studies.

claim: The VS-SF coupling is an accessory or modulatory gating mechanism.
source: pointing to the notion that it is an accessory or modulatory gating mechanism.
evidence: This is speculation based on the experimental observations.

claim: The alternative coupling mechanism might be more relevant in non-swapped domain channels such as from EAG K+ channels family.
source: Indeed, this alternative mechanism might be more relevant in non-swapped domain channels such as from ether-a-go-go (EAG) K+ channels family (EAG and hERG), which can open even without covalent interaction between the VSD and the PD (without the classical canonical coupling) (Lörinczi et al., 2015).
evidence: This is speculation based on knowledge from a cited study.

claim: EAG and hERG channels can open even without covalent interaction between the VSD and the PD.
source: which can open even without covalent interaction between the VSD and the PD (without the classical canonical coupling) (Lörinczi et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge from a previous study, supported by citation.

claim: Multiple non-covalent interactions between amino acid residues from the VSD and the PD can endow voltage dependence to the open probability of the PD.
source: This result suggests that the multiple non-covalent interactions between amino acid residues from the VSD and the PD can endow voltage dependence to the open probability of the PD.
evidence: This is inferred from the cited study about EAG channels.

claim: In hERG, a mutation at W568 has been proposed to be involved in a pathway that couples activation and inactivation.
source: Furthermore, in hERG a mutation at W568 has been previously proposed to be involved in a pathway that couples activation and inactivation and when mutated to Leu (W568L), the channel does not exhibit C-type inactivation (Ferrer et al., 2011).
evidence: This is established knowledge from a previous study, supported by citation.

claim: When W568 in hERG is mutated to Leu (W568L), the channel does not exhibit C-type inactivation.
source: and when mutated to Leu (W568L), the channel does not exhibit C-type inactivation (Ferrer et al., 2011).
evidence: This is established knowledge from a previous study, supported by citation.

claim: Residue W568 in hERG is homolog to residue S412 in Shaker.
source: Interestingly, residue W568 in hERG is homolog to residue S412 in Shaker demonstrating the physiological relevance of such alternative coupling mechanism in other members of K+ channels family.
evidence: This is based on sequence alignment and structural knowledge.

claim: The homology between W568 in hERG and S412 in Shaker demonstrates the physiological relevance of the alternative coupling mechanism in other members of K+ channels family.
source: demonstrating the physiological relevance of such alternative coupling mechanism in other members of K+ channels family.
evidence: This is inferred from the homology and the functional similarities.

claim: Residues L409, S411, S412, F433, and W434F comprise the molecular chain of residues that directly connects the voltage sensor to the SF gate in Shaker K+ channels.
source: In summary, we have shown that residues L409, S411, S412, F433, and W434F comprise the molecular chain of residues that directly connects the voltage sensor to the SF gate, in Shaker K+ channels.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study, supported by all the experimental data.

claim: The VS-SF coupling mechanism may play a role in other members of the voltage-gated ion channels superfamily, for example, NaV channels.
source: It is also possible that this mechanism is not only important in domain-swapped and non-swapped K+ channels, but also may play a role in other members of the voltage-gated ion channels superfamily, for example, NaV channels.
evidence: This is speculation about the broader applicability of the mechanism.

claim: Shaker zH4 K+ channel with fast inactivation removed (∆6–46) was used for the study.
source: Shaker zH4 K+ channel with fast inactivation removed (Hoshi et al., 1990), ∆6–46, and cloned into pBSTA vector was used.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental materials and methods.

claim: Mutations were performed using Quick-change II technology.
source: Mutations were performed using Quick-change II technology (Stratagene, La Jolla, CA), together with custom primers from Integrated DNA Technologies (Integrated DNA Technologies, Inc, Coralville, IA).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental methods.

claim: Oocytes were harvested from Xenopus laevis in accordance with experimental protocols approved by the University of Chicago IACUC.
source: Oocytes were harvested from Xenopus laevis in accordance with experimental protocols #71475 approved by the University of Chicago Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental procedures and ethical approval.

claim: Ionic and gating currents were recorded using cut-open oocyte voltage-clamp method.
source: Ionic and gating currents were recorded using cut-open oocyte voltage-clamp method (Stefani and Bezanilla, 1998).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental methods, supported by citation.
